summary: An August 2021 technical analysis of DTCC/NSCC settlement mechanics and their hypothesized effect on GameStop price movements. The author describes Supplementary Liquidity Deposit (SLD) cycles tied to monthly options expiration, T+calendar cycles (C+21, C+35 renamed from T+21/T+35), and mechanisms for hiding FTDs through CNS exemptions and reorganization (X-REORG) flags. The work speculates that RC/GameStop could trigger corporate events to force settlement of obligations and create a short squeeze, proposing NFT share-counting as a potential solution. The author expresses declining confidence in C+21 effectiveness while maintaining higher confidence in SLD cycle predictability, and is critical of DTCC/NSCC legacy systems.

key_claims.claim: Claims that SLD cycles tied to monthly options expiration (3rd Friday) create predictable and material GameStop price movements through netting and settlement effects, with 9/10 confidence
key_claims.note: Pages 3–10. While underlying SLD mechanics (deposit periods, CNS netting, settlement) are real and documented, the claim of predictable GME price causation is unproven. Author acknowledges many SLD cycles are 'nothingburgers.' Pattern recognition appears cherry-picked; no regulatory or market study supports predictive causation.

key_claims.claim: Claims that C+21 (renamed T+21) calendar-day cycles drive predictable GME price movements and represent margin-call indicators
key_claims.note: Pages 10–12. By the time of writing (Aug 2021), author admits C+21 'is in fact mostly horse shit' and 'effects of C+21 are too diminished to see them.' Author gave it only 3/10 confidence, contradicting the premise that it is a reliable price mechanism. No market evidence supports C+21 predictive power through mid-2026.

key_claims.claim: Claims that a bank holiday on January 18, 2021 disrupted CNS netting and that the next identical occurrence (February 21, 2022) will have comparable major GME implications
key_claims.note: Page 8. The prediction deadline (Feb 21, 2022) has passed. No notable GME market event or CNS disruption is documented for that date. The causal linkage (holiday → CNS disruption → major price effect) was speculative and failed to materialize.

key_claims.claim: Claims that Robinhood's January 28, 2021 margin call was caused or timed by SLD cycle mechanics and settlement operations
key_claims.note: Pages 8–9. RH was margin-called on Jan 28 (verifiable), but the SEC's October 2021 staff report concluded the Jan 2021 price run-up was driven primarily by positive-sentiment retail buying, not short-covering or settlement mechanics. Timing overlap appears coincidental, not causal.

key_claims.claim: Claims that FTDs can be legally hidden indefinitely through CNS exclusions (ODS exemptions and X-REORG flags) without forced buyins or regulatory intervention
key_claims.note: Pages 14–18. Author includes explicit warning: 'this part is not 100% verified.' While some exemptions exist in DTCC rules, the scale and persistence of this practice is unsubstantiated. No forced buyins or system collapse resulted as implied; DTCC/NSCC continue normal operations.

key_claims.claim: Claims that RC/GameStop can trigger a mandatory corporate event (merger, name change, cash reorganization) to force DTCC to liquidate all FTD obligations and create a 'MOASS'
key_claims.note: Pages 15–18. By mid-2026, no such corporate event has been triggered. GameStop completed a 4-for-1 stock split (via dividend) in July 2022, which did not trigger forced buyins or price spike consistent with MOASS theory. X-REORG exemptions, if real, appear to have held as author feared.

key_claims.claim: Claims that C+35 (renamed T+35) calendar cycles retain predictive power for GME price movements despite C+21 failure, with 4.5/10 confidence
key_claims.note: Pages 10–12. Author acknowledges C+35 'has diminished' and 'GME's harder to move.' Confidence rating of 4.5/10 is minimal. Through mid-2026, these cycles have not produced the predicted price effects; market moves on this stock are driven by company fundamentals, sentiment, and macroeconomic factors, not settlement cycles.

key_claims.claim: Claims that RC may use NFT-based share counting or an unspecified '4D chess' strategy to force final settlement of hidden obligations
key_claims.note: Page 18. GameStop launched an NFT marketplace in 2022 and shut it down in 2024 without resolving the claimed hidden obligations or triggering price action. The speculation proved unfounded; however, the prediction deadline (unspecified future) means cannot_assess rather than does_not_hold for the strictly temporal claim, though market evidence suggests inefficacy.

validity_rationale: The work documents real DTCC/NSCC settlement structures and real FTD/CNS mechanisms, which are factually accurate as background. However, its core thesis—that SLD and calendar cycles create predictable GME price movements culminating in forced buyback (MOASS)—fails under hindsight scrutiny. The SEC's October 2021 report contradicted the causal claim about Jan 2021 (sentiment-driven, not settlement-driven). By Aug 2021, the author already admitted C+21 was 'mostly horse shit,' indicating internal recognition of cycle failure. No corporate event forced buyins. GameStop's 2022 stock split produced no MOASS. The NFT solution materialized and dissolved without effect. Through mid-2026, short interest remained low, no margin calls on hedge funds occurred, and DTCC/NSCC systems remained stable. The work's accurate description of real mechanisms does not redeem its failed predictions and causal assertions."
